item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is materially closer to the frozen contract and much smaller in scope, while B directly violates several explicit API and scope requirements.","reasons":["A adds the required Upload method with the exact FilesOption signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and produces a replayable buffered body.","B changes the required signature to opts ...UploadFileOption, adds forbidden association/form-field options, and changes existing option return types.","B also refactors generic request/retry behavior and multipart helpers despite the contract explicitly excluding unrelated retry machinery changes.","A’s tests directly verify multipart name/content and retry from an os.File; B has broader tests but much of that coverage supports out-of-contract behavior."],"risks_a":["Upload calls a new private add method instead of routing through the existing Add method, violating the explicit reuse requirement.","Add now buffers every caller-provided body, changing its established streaming behavior rather than preserving it.","The added tests do not visibly cover Upload validation or source-reader failures, and validation collapses filename/content errors into one message."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong public signature and no longer accepts the contractually required ...FilesOption.","It duplicates Add’s request construction, decoding, and error handling instead of routing through Add.","It adds association fields and new option interfaces explicitly prohibited by the contract, creating unnecessary API surface and compatibility risk from changed option return types renderers may depend on behaviorally or in assignments/interfaces even if calls compile under gates, e.g. FilesOption-typed values from WithFilesQuery no longer assign directly without interface conversion rules? Actually return narrower composite is assignable to FilesOption, but static interface return changes API nevertheless. The patch also changes generic RawClient ownership/retry semantics and documentation far beyond scope. Tests do not visibly cover source-reader errors."]}
